{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1959)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=September 2026}}
{{Use American English|date=September 2026}}
'''Steven R. Finch''' (born 1959) is an American mathematician and research computing specialist known for work in experimental mathematics, mathematical constants, geometric probability, and computational mathematics. He is the author of the well-regarded reference books, ''Mathematical Constants'' (2003)<ref name="MC1">{{Cite web|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematical-constants|title=Mathematical Constants &#124; Mathematical Association of America|website=old.maa.org}}</ref> and ''Mathematical Constants II'' (2019),<ref name="MC2">{{Cite web|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematical-constants-ii|title=Mathematical Constants II &#124; Mathematical Association of America|website=old.maa.org}}</ref> both published by [[Cambridge University Press]].

==Early life, education, and career==
Raised in [[Midland, Michigan]], Finch was one of four children of Charles Richard Finch, a Dow Chemical engineer, and Shirley Peery Finch, a teacher.<ref name="Charles Finch obit">{{cite news |title=Charles R. Finch |work=Midland Daily News |date=May 7, 2019 |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/ourmidland/name/charles-finch-obituary?id=9614051 |via=Legacy.com |access-date=September 6, 2026}}</ref> As a teenager, Finch studied musical composition and won several state and regional composition competitions. From 1977 to 1978, he attended the [[Interlochen Arts Academy]] to study composition, and several of his works were performed, including a May 1978 recital of eight of his compositions, for which he served as the pianist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/midland-daily-news-finchs-work-to-be-pe/205412425/|title=Finch's work to be performed|date=April 26, 1978|pages=12|work=Midland Daily News|via=newspapers.com}}</ref>

He received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in Mathematics from [[Oberlin College]] in 1982,<ref name="MAA"/> where he was a member of [[Sigma Xi]] and [[Phi Beta Kappa]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/midland-daily-news-finch-joins-societies/205468846/|title=Finch Joins Societies|date=May 8, 1982|pages=28|work=Midland Daily News|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> and an [[Master of Science|M.S.]] in Applied Mathematics from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] in 1985.<ref name="MAA"/>

Early in his career, Finch worked at various times in statistical weather forecasting, technical editing, and biostatistics programming.<ref name="MAA"/>

==Research career==
Finch's research has included [[experimental mathematics]], [[combinatorial number theory]], [[geometric probability]], and problems involving mathematical constants. His early work examined additive integer sequences, including patterns and periodicity in 1-additive sequences and related [[sum-free set]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Finch |first=Steven R. |title=Patterns in 1-additive sequences |journal=Experimental Mathematics |volume=1 |issue=1 |year=1992 |pages=57–63}}</ref> He became interested in constants, and studied those arising in models of [[statistical mechanics]], including [[self-avoiding walk]]s, [[polyomino]]es, the [[Ising model]], and [[percolation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Finch |first=Steven R. |title=Several constants arising in statistical mechanics |journal=Annals of Combinatorics |volume=3 |year=1999 |pages=323–335}}</ref> Working with [[Irene Hueter]] on [[random convex hull]]s, Finch obtained an exact expression for a constant appearing in the asymptotic variance of the number of vertices of the convex hull of random points in a disk.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Finch |first1=Steven R. |last2=Hueter |first2=Irene |title=Random convex hulls: A variance revisited |journal=Advances in Applied Probability |volume=36 |issue=4 |year=2004 |pages=981–986 |doi=10.1017/S0001867800013276}}</ref>

Finch is the author of two positively reviewed reference books, ''Mathematical Constants'' (2003)<ref name="MC1"/> and ''Mathematical Constants II'' (2019),<ref name="MC2"/> both published by [[Cambridge University Press]]. The first book received favorable reviews in a number of mathematical publications. Writing in ''[[The Mathematical Intelligencer]]'', Jet Wimp concluded that "all mathematicians should own this book",<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wimp |first=Jet |title=Mathematical Constants |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |volume=26 |issue=2 |year=2004 |pages=70–74 |doi=10.1007/BF02985660}}</ref> while Gerry Leversha, in ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]'', described it as an "encyclopaedic feat of scholarship".<ref>{{cite journal |last=Leversha |first=Gerry |title=Mathematical constants, by Steven R. Finch |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=89 |issue=514 |year=2005 |pages=156–157 |doi=10.1017/S0025557200177228}}</ref> Reviewing both volumes in 2020, Osmo Pekonen compared Finch's achievement to the ''[[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]]'', describing the books as a collection of 269 "meticulously documented essays" and stating that Wimp's recommendation applied equally to ''Mathematical Constants II''.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Pekonen |first=Osmo |title=Mathematical Constants, Mathematical Constants II |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |volume=42 |year=2020 |pages=87–88 |doi=10.1007/s00283-019-09929-0}}</ref>

Finch received a [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] Book Fellowship beginning in 2004, and he and John Wetzel received the [[Lester R. Ford Award]] in 2005, given annually to "authors of articles of expository excellence" published in ''[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]'', the journal of the Mathematical Association of America.<ref name="MAA">{{cite web|url=https://maa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/PRZBK-MathFest2005.pdf |title=MathFest 2005: PRIZES and AWARDS|work=Mathematical Association of America|date=August 5, 2005}}</ref> The article for which the award was given surveyed a geometric minimization problem posed by [[Richard Bellman]], seeking the shortest path to guarantee a hiker's escape from a known closed convex region regardless of the hiker's initial position and direction.<ref name="MAA"/>

In addition to his work in mathematics, Finch has continued to compose and perform music as a classical pianist and choral singer. By 2003, he had released an album of his compositions, ''An Apple Gathering''.<ref name="MAA"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mit.edu/~sfinch/music/index.html|title=An Apple Gathering|website=www.mit.edu}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Finch is married to soprano Nancy Armstrong, with whom he also collaborated musically. Finch dedicated his 2003 book ''Mathematical Constants'' to Armstrong, writing, "For Nancy Armstrong, the one constant",<ref>{{cite book |last=Finch |first=Steven R. |title=Mathematical Constants |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2003 |isbn=978-0-521-81805-6 |url=https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781107266582_A24418080/preview-9781107266582_A24418080.pdf}}</ref> and a 2015 profile of Armstrong described her as "married to a mathematician",<ref>{{cite news |title=Armstrong is Ready to Entertain This Saturday for St. John's |work=Charlestown Patriot-Bridge |date=May 14, 2015 |url=https://charlestownbridge.com/2015/05/14/armstrong-is-ready-to-entertain-this-saturday-for-st-johns/ |access-date=September 6, 2026}}</ref> with late 2010s obituaries for Armstrong's brother-in-law and Finch's father identifying the pair as a couple.<ref name="Charles Finch obit"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Frederick Bolster |url=https://www.skidmore.edu/retirees/memoriam/2017/frederick-bolster.php |website=Skidmore College |date=2017 |access-date=September 6, 2026}}</ref>
